archive-python-package-verified.reason: Adopt for #218 (Part of #155). bench-tools archive check-packages reads a package written as evidence_store.pack writes one through bench_tools::archive and verifies each member's name, size, mode and SHA-256 against the manifest, after the archive's own size and SHA-256, as evidence_store.unpack does. evidence_store.unpack restores this fixture under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. The command is new, so its report format has no Python counterpart.

archive-multi-member-gzip-verified.reason: Adopt for #218 (Part of #155). Python's gzip reads every gzip member and skips zero bytes after each; bench_tools::archive reads members the same way, so a package split across gzip members with zero padding verifies. evidence_store.unpack restores this fixture under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7.

archive-python-scratch-verified.reason: Adopt for #218 (Part of #155). bench-tools archive check-scratch reads a native scratch archive written as native_artifacts.file_artifacts writes one and checks that each entry hashes to its name, as native_artifacts.verify's archive loop does. That loop accepts this fixture under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. Without the attempt's index, the entry limit is what the archive's size can hold.

archive-pax-global-header-refused.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6, which names this refusal). Old: evidence_store.unpack, through tarfile, accepts a package that begins with a PAX global header and applies its records to every later member; Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7 both restore this fixture. New: bench_tools::archive refuses it with "archive has a PAX global header", so check-packages reports the package and exits 1. Rationale: a global header changes later members' metadata from outside their own headers, and neither tarfile's default writer nor bench_tools::archive emits one. Compatibility: none of the 33 published packages has one (docs/python-migration/evidence/published-packages.2026-10-19.json); a package with one would be refused rather than restored. Resolved by #218.

archive-gnu-sparse-refused.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6: readers refuse non-regular members by type). Old: tarfile counts a GNU sparse member ('S') as a regular file and evidence_store.unpack restores its expanded bytes; Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7 both restore this fixture. New: bench_tools::archive refuses a GNU sparse member, and any member whose PAX records carry GNU.sparse keys, with "archive member is sparse". Rationale: the tar crate does not expand PAX sparse members, so reading their stored bytes as file content would silently differ from Python; refusing both forms keeps one rule, and no writer of ours emits sparse members. Compatibility: none of the 33 published packages has a sparse member; one would be refused rather than restored. Resolved by #218.

archive-pax-size-refused.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6 and its metadata limits). Old: tarfile takes a member's size from a PAX size record over its header, and evidence_store.unpack restores this fixture, whose records equal the header sizes, under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: bench_tools::archive refuses any PAX size record with "archive member has a PAX size record". Rationale: the reader walks headers itself so it can cap name records before the tar crate allocates, and in that mode the crate advances by the header size; honoring a different PAX size would desynchronize it, and tarfile writes a size record only for members of 8 GiB or more, above the 2 GiB package limit. Compatibility: none of the 33 published packages has one; no package within the asset limit needs one. Resolved by #218.

archive-gzip-crc-after-end-marker-refuse.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6: the readers return typed errors for a bad CRC). Old: tarfile stops reading at the tar end marker, so Python's gzip checks the trailer only when its read buffer happens to reach it; with 512 KiB after the end marker, evidence_store.unpack restores this fixture despite its wrong CRC under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: bench_tools::archive parses no entry after the end marker but reads the rest of the decoded stream through its byte limit, so every gzip member's CRC and length are checked and this package is refused with "corrupt gzip stream does not have a matching checksum". Rationale: integrity no longer depends on buffer sizes. Compatibility: the archive's SHA-256 is checked against its manifest first, so a published package cannot change; all 33 read with their trailers checked. Resolved by #218.

archive-invalid-header-after-members-ref.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6: malicious archives keep their refusals). Old: tarfile treats an invalid or truncated header anywhere after the first as the end of the archive, so evidence_store.unpack restores this fixture, whose end marker is replaced by a header with a wrong checksum, under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: bench_tools::archive, through the tar crate, refuses it with "archive header checksum mismatch"; only an all-zero block ends the archive. Rationale: a damaged header is damage, not an end marker. Compatibility: none of the 33 published packages has one; the archive SHA-256 check already rules out a changed package. Resolved by #218.

archive-extension-header-over-limit-refu.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6: each PAX or GNU name record is capped at 64 KiB before the crates allocate). Old: tarfile reads a PAX header of any size, and evidence_store.unpack restores this fixture, whose first member's PAX header holds a 70,000-byte comment, under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: bench_tools::archive refuses any PAX header, GNU long name or GNU long link over 65536 bytes from its header, before reading it, with "archive extension header of N bytes exceeds 65536 bytes". Rationale: the cap bounds allocation by the index instead of by the archive; the limit covers the whole record set, whatever its keys. Compatibility: all 33 published packages read under this cap (docs/python-migration/evidence/published-packages.2026-10-19.json); a package with a larger extension header would be refused rather than restored. Resolved by #218.

archive-gzip-header-field-over-limit-ref.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 1: archives use pinned crates, each behavior difference with a decision and a case; shared decision 6: metadata limits). Old: Python's gzip skips an FNAME or FCOMMENT field of any length, so evidence_store.unpack restores this fixture, whose FNAME is 70,000 bytes, under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: flate2 1.1.10's gzip header parser stops at 65,535 bytes per field, so bench_tools::archive refuses the package with "gzip header field too long". Rationale: the cap bounds the header buffer the crate keeps; evidence_store.pack and bench_tools::archive write no FNAME at all. Compatibility: all 33 published packages read under this cap (docs/python-migration/evidence/published-packages.2026-10-19.json), and evidence_store.pack writes GzipFile(filename=''), which sets no FNAME; a gzip stream with a longer field would be refused rather than read. Resolved by #218.

archive-zip64-extensible-data-over-limit.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6: zip end records are read first and refused above their limits before ZipArchive opens). Old: zipfile reads a zip64 end record with extensible data of any size, and native_artifacts.verify's archive loop accepts this fixture, whose zip64 end record carries 70,000 bytes of extensible data behind 0xFFFF/0xFFFFFFFF markers, under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: when a 32-bit end record defers to zip64, bench_tools::archive refuses a zip64 end record with more than 65,536 bytes of extensible data, before ZipArchive allocates it, with "zip64 end record carries N bytes of extensible data, above 65536". Rationale: the zip crate reads the extensible data into memory, so its size is metadata the index must bound. Compatibility: both tracked native-scratch.v1.zip files have no zip64 records; zipfile writes none with extensible data. Resolved by #218.

archive-zip-bzip2-refused.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6, which names this refusal). Old: zipfile reads bzip2 entries, and native_artifacts.verify's archive loop accepts this fixture under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: bench_tools::archive refuses any compression method other than stored and deflate with "archive member uses compression method Bzip2, not stored or deflate"; the zip crate's method name is shown. Rationale: native_artifacts.file_artifacts writes deflate only, and the crate is built with deflate alone. Compatibility: both tracked native-scratch.v1.zip files use deflate only. Resolved by #218.

archive-zip-symlink-entry-refused.reason: Intended change for #218, authority #155 (delivery plan, shared decision 6: readers refuse non-regular members by type and mode bits). Old: zipfile ignores external attributes, so native_artifacts.verify's archive loop accepts an entry with Unix symlink mode bits under Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. New: bench_tools::archive refuses a zip entry whose Unix mode names a directory, symbolic link or other special file, or whose name ends in a slash, with "archive member is not a regular file". Rationale: the same rule as for tar members; restoration takes modes from the storage record, never from the zip. Compatibility: both tracked native-scratch.v1.zip files hold mode 0600 regular entries. Resolved by #218.
